title: ERM++: An Improved Baseline for Domain Generalization
mechanism: A tuned plain-ERM recipe: average all weight iterates (MPA), warm-start the new head on a frozen backbone, set training length on val then retrain on train+val, stronger init, unfrozen BN.
adaptation: MPA as a running mean of all U-Net++ weights from step 2k to 20k with BN stats recomputed on train; warm start = PF's 1k frozen steps; fix the schedule (plateau lr drops, cap 80k) on the module-grouped 5-fold CV, then retrain the final model on all 532 train+val cells.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + MPA (same run, paired raw vs averaged), then PF + MPA + full-data retrain. Baseline: SUP100-PF, seeds 5-9. Metric: val/CV crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, then test clean crack relF1@2, E1 crack relF1@2, E1 inactive IoU. Kill: MPA minus raw < +0.005 val relF1@2 paired over 5 seeds and E1 inactive not better.
evidence: R (full text, Table 2a, ResNet-50, 5 DomainBed datasets): ERM++ 68.9 avg; without MPA 65.9 (-3.0, largest), without full data 67.7, without strong init 67.6, without unfrozen BN 68.3, without Auto-LR 68.4, without warm start 68.7.
prior_overlap: BRIEF section 5 optimizer row: EMA/SWA and longer schedules never varied; PF covers only the warm-start part. Open.
